content: 1. P3A inhibitors should be used with caution. Reduce the dose of capivasertib and monitor for adverse effects when co-administered. 2. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. 3. Cobicistat increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the ceritinib dose by approximately 33%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor, resume the previous ceritinib dose. 4. Cobicistat and ceritinib may increase each other's toxicity via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration may also increase QT prolongation risk. 5. Chloramphenicol increases atazanavir and cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Atazanavir increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration with bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as this may exacerbate bile salt accumulation in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin. 7. Cobicistat and clarithromycin increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases cobicistat levels; avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Cimetidine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. For treatment-naïve patients, take atazanavir simultaneously with the H2-receptor antagonist (H2RA) or at least 10 hours afterward. Adjust dosages for treatment-experienced patients. 9. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after these medications. 10. Cobicistat increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and atazanavir increases cobicistat levels similarly. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Atazanavir increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If co-administration is necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Colchicine is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 12. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 13. Cobicistat increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Increased crizotinib levels may prolong QT intervals. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the crizotinib dose to 250 mg once daily. 14. Atazanavir increases dabrafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases dabrafenib levels similarly, while dabrafenib decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Cobicistat increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir increases daridorexant levels similarly. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Cobicistat increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir increases cobicistat levels similarly. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Dexlansoprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) should not exceed doses comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 18. Dexamethasone decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with corticosteroids that induce CYP3A4 may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance to atazanavir or darunavir. Cobicistat increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Long-term use of corticosteroids metabolized by CYP3A may increase the risk of systemic corticosteroid effects, including Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. 19. Cobicistat increases dihydroergotamine intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Cobicistat increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Atazanavir increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Cobicistat increases edoxaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 23. Efavirenz decreases atazanavir and cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with efavirenz may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance to cobicistat. 24. Cobicistat increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir increases elacestrant levels similarly. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Cobicistat increases elbasvir/grazoprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of elbasvir/grazoprevir with certain strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 26. Atazanavir increases eluxadoline levels by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg twice daily if co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 27. Cobicistat increases entrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 28. Cobicistat increases enzalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while enzalutamide decreases atazanavir levels. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Cobicistat increases erdafitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, consider increasing the erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 30. Atazanavir increases ergoloid mesylates levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Cobicistat and erythromycin base increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is co-administered with atazanavir or darunavir. 32. Atazanavir increases ergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Atazanavir increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Atazanavir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is co-administered with atazanavir or darunavir. 35. Cobicistat and erythromycin lactobionate increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Atazanavir increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat and erythromycin stearate increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is co-administered with atazanavir or darunavir. 37. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative anticonvulsant or antiretroviral therapy to avoid potential changes in exposures. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. 38. Esomeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. PPIs should not exceed doses comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 39. Cobicistat increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Atazanavir may alter ethinylestradiol levels, leading to significant changes in estrogen plasma levels. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method. 41. Etravirine decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Famotidine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
